slot.brief: Diagram of a wheel rolling without slipping; relate speed of a marked point on the rim to translational speed, or find acceleration of the contact point.

stem: A wheel of radius $R$ rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface such that its centre moves with a constant speed $v$, as shown in the figure. At the instant shown, a point $P$ on the rim is at a height $\dfrac{3R}{2}$ above the ground. The speed of point $P$ relative to the ground is

verdicts.working: Rolling without slipping: ω = v/R, contact point is instantaneous axis. P at height 3R/2 has coordinates relative to contact point (√3R/2, 3R/2), so distance from contact = √(3R²/4 + 9R²/4) = √3 R. Speed = ω·√3R = √3 v. Confirmed by vector addition: v_P = (3v/2, −√3v/2), magnitude √3 v.

working:
Method 1 (Instantaneous Centre of Rotation):
In rolling without slipping on a stationary horizontal surface, the point of contact $O$ with the ground is the instantaneous centre of zero velocity (ICR). The angular velocity of the wheel is:
$$\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$$

The speed of any point on the wheel is proportional to its distance from the contact point $O$:
$$v_P = \omega \cdot d$$
Taking the contact point $O$ as the origin $(0, 0)$, the circle is described by:
$$x^2 + (y - R)^2 = R^2 \implies x^2 + y^2 = 2Ry$$
The distance $d$ of point $P$ from the contact point $O$ is:
$$d = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{2Ry}$$
Given $y = \dfrac{3R}{2}$:
$$d = \sqrt{2R\left(\dfrac{3R}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{3}R$$
Therefore, the speed of point $P$ is:
$$v_P = \omega \cdot d = \left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)(\sqrt{3}R) = \sqrt{3}v$$

Method 2 (Vector Addition):
$$\vec{v}_P = \vec{v}_C + \vec{v}_{P/C}$$
Here $|\vec{v}_C| = v$ horizontally, and $|\vec{v}_{P/C}| = \omega R = v$ tangential to the rim.
Since the vertical coordinate relative to the centre is $y' = \dfrac{R}{2}$, the radius vector makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal ($\sin 30^\circ = 1/2$).
The tangent makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the horizontal velocity $\vec{v}_C$. Using the law of cosines for vector addition:
$$v_P = \sqrt{v^2 + v^2 + 2v^2\cos 60^\circ} = \sqrt{v^2 + v^2 + 2v^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{3}v$$

Independent check: Rolling without slipping: ω = v/R, contact point is instantaneous axis. Confirmed by vector addition: v_P = (3v/2, −√3v/2), magnitude √3 v.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A ($v$): Corresponds to a sign error in vector addition, taking $\cos(120^\circ)$ instead of $\cos(60^\circ)$, giving $\sqrt{v^2 + v^2 - v^2} = v$, or confusing the condition with $h = R/2$.

Option D ($2v$): Corresponds to taking the speed of the topmost point on the wheel ($h = 2R$), where translational and rotational velocities are parallel.

figure.description: A circular wheel of radius $R$ is shown rolling on a horizontal ground line with hatching below. The center of the wheel is labeled $C$. A horizontal arrow pointing to the right from center $C$ is labeled with velocity $v$. A curved clockwise arrow near the top of the wheel indicates rolling without slipping. The lowest point of the wheel touches the ground line. A point $P$ is marked with a solid dot on the rim in the upper-right quadrant. A horizontal dashed line extends rightward from point $P$, and a vertical dimension line with arrows measures the vertical distance from the ground line up to this dashed line, labeled with the value $\dfrac{3R}{2}$. A dashed vertical line from center $C$ down to the ground is labeled $R$.
